channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Could Robots Be K-pop's Next Stars?
item.description: AI is transforming South Korea's entertainment industry, with one startup betting on physical AI in the race to create the superstars of the future. Galaxy Corporation sees robot idols as the next generation of K-pop celebrities. Bloomberg's Sohee Kim reports from Seoul. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple to Launch New Mac Mini; AirPods 5 and OLED iPad Mini Timing Details
item.description: Apple Inc. is gearing up to launch a new version of its Mac mini desktop computer for the first time in almost two years, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: SK Hynix Union Rejects Preliminary Wage Hike Deal, Yonhap Says
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s union rejected an agreement that would have raised salaries and paid out a portion of bonuses in company shares, Yonhap News reported.
item.dc:creator: Shinhye Kang

item.title: AI Cloud Provider Lambda in Talks for $3 Billion Pre-IPO Round
item.description: Lambda Inc., an AI cloud-computing provider backed by Nvidia Corp., is in talks to raise as much as $3 billion in a round that could tee it up to go public next year, according to people familiar with the efforts.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz, Natasha Mascarenhas and Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Markets Slip as Nvidia, Yields & the Debasement Trade Loom | The Close 8/24/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Principal Asset Management CEO & President Kamal Bhatia, Tether Co-Founder Bill Quigley, Goldman Sachs Research US Software Equity Research Analyst Gabriela Borges, Bilt CEO Ankur Jain & Equinox Group Executive Chairman Harvey Spevak, GenTrust Head of NY Office, Senior Client Advisor Mimi Duff, Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok, Hartree Partners Senior Advisor Ed Morse, Columbia Threadneedle Investments Portfolio Manager Ed Al-Hussainy, & Canada Chamber of Commerce Principal Economist Andrew DiCapua. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tether Co-Founder on Bitcoin's Bounce, Clarity Act Hopes
item.description: Bill Quigley, Co-Founder of Tether and Wax, explains that Bitcoin is increasingly behaving like a gold hedge against U.S. government inflation, with its correlation to gold rising to 0.71. This shift has contributed to Bitcoin's 35% increase since June lows. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Smart Ring Maker Oura Seeks to Raise Up to $3 Billion in US IPO
item.description: Oura Health Oy, a maker of smart rings that track health, fitness and sleep, and some of its backers are seeking to raise as much as $3 billion in a US IPO, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz and Mark Gurman

item.title: Nuclear Power Demand Driven by AI, Hyperscaler Companies, Says TerraPower CEO
item.description: TerraPower CEO Chris Levesque said that hyperscalers are driving demand for nuclear power companies, as his company is set to announce a deal with a data center customer for a new nuclear power plant this year. Levesque, who was joined by Bloomberg News energy reporter Will Wade, also said that TerraPower is aiming to get construction time and consumer costs lower so that nuclear can become a larger energy source for the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto’s 24/7 Markets Take Aim at Wall Street
item.description: Crypto is pushing traditional markets toward a world where trading never stops. Trade.xyz, a little-known market built on top of crypto exchange Hyperliquid, has generated roughly $500 billion in volume since launching in October, with perpetual futures tied to assets ranging from oil and gold to the S&P 500 and pre-IPO companies such as SpaceX. The platform and Hyperliquid are now pushing regulators to allow pre-IPO perps in the US, arguing they could improve price discovery. Bloomberg's Muyao Shen joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Cuts Jobs as It Reprioritizes Around AI
item.description: Apple is cutting jobs across its Vision Pro, Siri, and Intelligent Systems Experiences teams as it redirects resources toward new devices and artificial intelligence. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman explains where the reductions are happening and how Apple is reshaping its Siri operation around new AI infrastructure. He also looks ahead to Apple’s foldable iPhone and why the device could prove particularly important in China. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Customers Brace for Higher AI Costs
item.description: Nvidia customers are being warned of potential price increases of around 15% for Blackwell and Rubin-based AI systems as soaring memory costs ripple through the infrastructure buildout. Raymond James Analyst and Managing Director Simon Leopold explains why the increases aren’t surprising and why older generations of GPUs can remain valuable even as newer chips enter production. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Rising Price of the AI Race | Bloomberg Tech 8/24/2026
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down what to expect from Nvidia's earnings this week, this as Bloomberg reports Nvidia customers have been notified about price hikes. Plus, SoftBank plans a record $6.3 billion retail bond sale to raise funds for its investment commitments to OpenAI. And, Alibaba raises $10.2 billion to take the lead in the global AI race in what was Hong Kong's biggest follow-on offering. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Markets Eye Bessent, Warsh, Nvidia | Open Interest 8/24/2026
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Treasuries extend their rally as Wall Street games out Bessent's next move ahead of Jackson Hole. Nvidia takes the earnings spotlight as rising costs loom over those results later this week. Canada braces for a long US trade war, while Washington warns an "economic D-Day" is coming for Iran. Plus, Protolabs CEO Suresh Krishna on the manufacturing boom fueled by growing demand across defense, aerospace and data centers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China’s Hackers Use DeepSeek for Attacks, Researchers Say
item.description: Chinese hackers are ramping up attacks after integrating DeepSeek and other open-source artificial intelligence models into their operations, highlighting attackers’ ability to leverage basic AI tools to hit targets abroad.
item.dc:creator: Mark Anderson

item.title: Trump's Family Joins the Sprint to Get a National Bank Charter
item.description: Donald Trump's family has won preliminary approval to start a national bank, riding a wave of deregulation under the Trump administration. Bloomberg's Paige Smith joins Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: LinkedIn Users Are Rewriting the Past to Land Jobs
item.description: Researchers at Stanford University and Revelio Labs found that nearly 20% of established US LinkedIn users edited the descriptions or titles of jobs they had left years earlier, with tech workers doing so at a rate of nearly one in three. These changes, dubbed "time travel," aren't made while memories are still fresh, but instead reflect a change in personal branding, with the median time-travel edit occurring more than four years after the user left the role. Beth Kowitt, Bloomberg Opinion Columnist covering corporate America joined Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Taiwan Indicts Nvidia Manager Following Chip Smuggling Probe
item.description: Taiwanese prosecutors indicted a senior Nvidia Corp. manager as part of a group that allegedly smuggled advanced AI chips into China, according to people familiar with the matter, advancing the island democracy’s first known crackdown on the black-market trade of such accelerators.
item.dc:creator: Mackenzie Hawkins

item.title: Australia Data-Center Power Use Seen Up Sevenfold by 2036
item.description: Australia sees data-center electricity use rising almost sevenfold over the next decade, highlighting the need for investment in generation and storage as the nation’s aging coal plants are retired.
item.dc:creator: Keira Wright

item.title: Temu Owner PDD Misses on Second-Quarter Sales, Beats on Earnings
item.description: PDD Holdings Inc., owner of the global e-commerce marketplace Temu, posted second-quarter sales that missed Wall Street’s expectations, overshadowing what was otherwise a strong beat on earnings.
item.dc:creator: Jake Rudnitsky

item.title: ByteDance Challenges Tencent With New Doubao Workplace AI Agent
item.description: ByteDance Ltd. launched a workspace AI agent under the brand of China’s most popular chatbot, entering a burgeoning domestic market to take on Tencent Holdings Ltd.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
